skills.name: Writing: how young people can improve their community

note.text:
Writing two paragraphs:
• Paragraph one: the problems in the community and why young people should help (for example, dirty streets, blocked gutters, children who cannot read, lonely old people).
• Paragraph two: what young people can do, with examples (clean-up campaigns, planting trees, helping younger children with homework, visiting the sick, avoiding drugs and violence).
Each paragraph has a topic sentence and supporting sentences.
Use should and can for suggestions: “Young people should …” “We can …”
Linking words: first, also, in addition, for example, because, finally.
End with a strong closing sentence.

worked_example.problem: Write the topic sentences of the two paragraphs about young people in {t}.
steps: Paragraph one (problems): Our quarter in {t} has dirty gutters and many children who need help with school.
Paragraph two (actions): Young people can do a lot to make {t} a better place.
Each topic sentence is followed by examples and reasons, with should, can and linking words.
worked_example.answer: Problems and why we should help → what young people can do, with examples.

cards.idea: Each paragraph starts with a topic sentence; the other sentences support it.
example: Topic: “Young people can make our town cleaner.”
Support: “For example, we can clean the gutters every month.”

check.prompt: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about what young people can do?

cards.idea: Use should and can to make suggestions.
example: We can help younger children with their homework.

cards.idea: Linking words make the paragraph flow: first, also, in addition, for example, finally.
example: First, we can clean the market.
In addition, we can plant trees along the road.

questions.prompt: Choose the linking word that fits.

paper_task.prompt: Write two paragraphs in your exercise book on the topic “How young people can improve life in their community”. In the first paragraph describe the problems; in the second, say what young people can do, with examples. Use should or can, and at least three linking words.
model: Our community has many problems. The gutters are often blocked with rubbish, so the streets flood when it rains. Some children cannot read well because nobody helps them at home, and some old people live alone. Young people should help, because this is our home and our future.

There are many things young people can do. First, we can organise a clean-up campaign every month to clear the gutters and the market. In addition, older pupils can teach younger children to read after school. We can also visit old people and fetch water for them. Finally, we should avoid drugs and violence and be good examples. If we work together, our community will be cleaner, safer and happier.
checklist: Each paragraph starts with a topic sentence.
Paragraph one describes problems; paragraph two gives actions with examples.
I used at least three linking words.
I ended with a strong closing sentence.
I checked capital letters, full stops and spelling.
